newsitem.title: UK: YEAREND-Taiwan stocks seen boosted by Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: YEAREND-Taiwan stocks seen boosted by Hong Kong.

text.p: Brokers made optimistic forecasts on Taiwan's 1997 stock market performance mainly because of an expected improving economy and anticipated bullish "greater China" market after Hong Kong's return to China next July.
A Reuters survey of 10 forecasts for the Taiwanese stock market showed the TAIEX index rising to an average of 7,950, a hefty 16 percent increase on the December 10 close of 6841.03.
The highest forecast was 9,500 and the lowest 6,500.
Following are a selection of views on next year's performance of the Taiwan stock exchange:
MICHAEL HUNG, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT NIKKO SECURITIES

"A bullish greater China market due to China's commitment on Hong Kong's return and (anticipated) direct shipping links with Taiwan is one of the three reasons that lead us to believe that Taiwan will be a bullish market for the next three years."
ALEX CHIU, TRADING MANAGER AT CAPITAL SECURITIES
"After Hong Kong's return to China, I believe Taiwan and China will enter intensive cooperation to benefit the bilateral economy.
"The domestic real estate market also will mount a strong recovery in the latter half of 1997, becoming a locomotive to boost both the economy and the stock market."
